title: Company staffing surge contingency and townline notes v0.1
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working notes + lightweight playbook for the potential mid-year staffing surge scenario we discussed in Exec Ops. It combines: 1) quick decision triggers, 2) exec-level asks and approvals we would need, 3) a concise townline/town-hall run-of-show and talking points, and 4) the short list of OKR tweaks we should consider if headcount ramp accelerates.

Status and context:
- Draft (v0.1): working notes oriented toward exec alignment.
- Background: Hiring momentum has accelerated in product and infra; recruiting indicates a potential to ramp +30 FTEs in Q3 if we clear two approvals: near-term budget carve-out and adjusted hiring velocity headroom for Dedicated/Private teams. This doc captures the coordination we need.

Decision triggers (binary checkpoints):
- Trigger A (go/no-go): Recruiting pipeline shows 50+ screened candidates with offers ready in 3 weeks AND 80% of priority roles reachable by our preferred comp bands.
- Trigger B (funding guardrail): Finance confirms a one-time draw from operating reserves up to $X for ramp hiring (proposal: 3 months of incremental run rate).
- Trigger C (capacity constraint): SRE/Infra certify that we can onboard 10 new engineers/week to non-critical squads without causing pager overload.
- If A+B+C are all true, we move to Surge Stage 1; otherwise pause and re-evaluate in two weeks.

Surge staging and timeline (high level):
- Stage 0 (monitor): open for two weeks to validate Recruiting funnel.
- Stage 1 (rapid offers): mobilize People Ops + Hiring Managers; target 50% offers accepted within 30 days.
- Stage 2 (onboarding push): shift Dedicated/Private onboarding templates to fast-track, 2-week bootcamp for new hires.
- Stage 3 (stabilize): freeze new offers and switch to normal pace once 30-day retention >85% and SRE sign-off.

Exec asks (what we need from leadership):
- CFO/Finance: sign-off on one-time $X reserve (exact figure in linked spreadsheet) and a commit-to-monthly headcount cadence for budgeting.
- CEO: authorize public/internal townline to staff + customers explaining the ramp and why it's safe for product stability.
- CTO/Eng leads: ratify the onboarding plan and approve temporary shift of 6 SRE hours/week for onboarding support.
- People Ops: confirm expedited offer approvals and temporary hiring panel rules to reduce time-to-offer by 30%.

Townline / All-hands run-of-show (30–40 minutes, target company-wide):
1) Quick framing (CEO, 3 min): why we might ramp, high-level benefits and fiscal guardrails.
2) What triggers we’re watching (COO/Head of Recruiting, 5 min): short checklist and timeline.
3) Impact on teams & customers (CTO, 6 min): how service stability is protected; Dedicated/Private customer commitments.
4) People Ops + Hiring ops (5 min): what this means for interviews, timelines, and manager expectations.
5) Fireside Q&A (CTO + People Ops + CFO, 10–15 min): pre-seeded questions + live.
6) Closing and next steps (CEO, 2 min): commitments and where to find the hiring dashboard.

Townline talking points (bullet bank):
- "We are monitoring a candidate funnel that could accelerate hiring while keeping our unit economics intact."
- "Any ramp will only happen if finance and ops give the green light — we will not compromise SLAs."
- "We will centralize onboarding effort for the first 8 weeks to reduce manager burden."
- "If we proceed, expect targeted hiring in product, infra, and SRE first; marketing and CS remain steady."

Draft slide deck outline (4–6 slides):
- Slide 1: TL;DR decision timeline + triggers
- Slide 2: Hiring funnel snapshot + priority roles by team
- Slide 3: Financial guardrails and expected incremental run rate
- Slide 4: Onboarding & SRE support plan
- Slide 5: Risks & mitigations (retention, cost, service impact)
- Slide 6: Key asks and next steps

Proposed short-term OKR adjustments (only if Surge moves forward):
- Replace: "Engineering: reduce average time-to-deploy by 20%" with "Engineering: maintain 99.9% critical path uptime during ramp." Rationale: prioritize stability while onboarding new engineers.
- Add: "People Ops: reduce time-to-offer for priority roles to <18 days for Q3."
- Add: "Hiring Ops: achieve 80% offer acceptance for top-tier candidates within 30 days."
- Flag for review: revisions to headcount-linked OKR targets will be presented to ELT after Trigger A validation.

Risks and mitigations (highlighted):
- Risk: New hire churn increases with accelerated pace -> Mitigation: 2-week cohort-based onboarding and mentorship pairing.
- Risk: On-call stress -> Mitigation: temporary shift swaps and bump in SRE support for first 60 days.
- Risk: Cost profile overshoots -> Mitigation: finance stop-gate after 60 days with retention review.

Operational checklist (what People Ops + Hiring Ops needs to execute):
- Freeze non-priority requisitions for 2 weeks to focus interviewers.
- Temporary interview rotation schedule; 3 interview-day templates.
- Onboarding curriculum ready: infra access, local stack, 2-week learning plan, mentor pairing.
- Weekly pulse metric dashboard: offers made, offers accepted, 30-day retention, time-to-offer, SRE onboarding incidents.

Communications plan (internal & external):
- Internal: townline + readout doc; update hr-hiring channel with weekly dashboards; managers get a short FAQ.
- External (customers): coordinated note for Dedicated/Private customers if onboarding activity might affect scheduled migrations; CS lead to pre-draft messages.

Action owners (first pass):
- People Ops: Lena Ortiz (lead) -> finalize fast-track offer flow and onboarding curriculum.
- Recruiting: Michael Chen -> present validated funnel and candidate list for Trigger A.
- Finance: Ravi Singh -> confirm reserve amount and stop-gate triggers.
- Engineering: Jordan Miles -> SRE capacity sign-off and onboarding support plan.
- CEO office: Asha Patel -> townline schedule and speaker coordination.

Open questions / unresolved items (quick list):
- Exact $X number for reserve (finance to propose by next ELT).
- Temporary changes to offer approvals: what threshold for exec-level override?
- Do we need to pause other projects to reassign mentors? If yes, which ones?

Next steps (two-week horizon):
- This doc -> ELT read & comment (by EOD Friday).
- Recruiting to present funnel evidence (Michael) in two business days.
- Finance to post proposed reserve math and a 60-day stop-gate plan (Ravi) in three business days.
- If all items green, schedule townline for next Wednesday; 72-hour prep cadence for speakers.

Appendix (links & reference):
- Hiring funnel export (linked_artifacts)
- Onboarding curriculum draft (drive link)
- Prior city-scale hiring retrospective (few months ago) with lessons learned

Notes to reviewers (meta):
- This is intentionally lean; want exec inputs on 1) reserve number, 2) SRE onboarding bandwidth, and 3) whether we should run a limited pilot (10 hires) before full surge.
- If we move to Stage 1 we will publish a separate, fuller surge playbook with day-by-day onboarding checklists and manager scripts.

-- end of v0.1 --
